title: Shopping & Payments
description: Convenience stores, shops and the checkout script you'll hear a hundred times.

phrases.registerNotes: Point and say it. Covers most of shopping on its own.
Bags are chargeable everywhere now, so you'll be asked every single time.
You may be given a face cover to put on first — that's standard, not a comment on you.
Needs your passport and a minimum spend. 免税 on a shop window means they do it.
Polite way to decline help without ending the interaction. Staff will leave you be.
Recognition only — you never say this, you only ever receive it. No reply is expected; a nod is plenty.
phrases.animeNote: Anime uses it accurately, but tends to skip that it needs no response. Answering it is the giveaway.

phrases.japanese: もう少し安いのはありますか
phrases.romaji: mō sukoshi yasui no wa arimasu ka
phrases.english: Is there anything a bit cheaper?
phrases.registerNotes: Asking for a cheaper option is fine. Haggling on price is not — prices are fixed almost everywhere.
phrases.audioHint: もうすこしやすいのはありますか

phrases.japanese: 他のサイズはありますか

furigana.b: のサイズはありますか

phrases.romaji: hoka no saizu wa arimasu ka
phrases.registerNotes: Japanese sizing runs small by Western standards — expect to go up one or two.
phrases.audioHint: ほかのサイズはありますか

phrases.japanese: ポイントカードはお持ちですか
phrases.romaji: pointo kādo wa o-mochi desu ka
phrases.english: Do you have a point card?
phrases.registerNotes: Recognition only, but you will be asked this at literally every till. Answer いいえ、大丈夫です.
phrases.audioHint: ポイントカードはおもちですか

phrases.registerNotes: Recognition only — asked at every convenience store when you buy a bento or bun. はい、お願いします or 大丈夫です.
